Winnie Mandela 2

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A new documentary about her life has sparked heated debate about the tarnished reputation of Winnie Madikizela Mandela

Unique Selling Point:
The documentary, which has won an international award, has many believing that Madikizela-Mandela was completely innocent of the crimes she's long been under suspicion of committing. But it was a one sided story, told by a filmmaker and as was her right to do, it painted a very specific picture. Embarrassingly for the ANC, it has emerged that they were just as complicit in tarnishing Mandela's name.

Summary:
The uncontested fact remains that Winnie Mandela was found guilty in a court of law for the abduction and kidnapping of Stompie Seipei, and received a 6 year sentence for the crime. On appeal that was eventually changed to two years suspended sentence. It is also a well known and uncontested fact that Mandela United FC were not choir boys, and while there is no evidence of just how much of what they did was actually under her orders, she didn't do anything to stop their reign of terror in Soweto. And that is really the crux of the story - while it is clear and quite frankly obvious that Mandela was the target of Apartheid propoganda and smear campaigns, and while she was treated inhumanly cruel by the regime, she was also a flawed character who was at least, according to the law, partly responsible for the death of Stompie.

Press Release:


Winnie Madikizela-Mandela II
From accusations of assault and kidnapping to secret operatives assisting the apartheid government to destroy her name – the story of Winnie Madikizela-Mandela has always been highly contested. Now an explosive documentary about the late struggle icon has unlocked new questions regarding her legacy. Carte Blanche analyses this developing story.


Script:


Winnie 2
20 April 2018



Sound Up HRH Zenani Mandela-Dlamini

Voice
It’s been nearly three weeks since the passing of one of South Africa’s most recognisable political figures. As in so much of her life, Winnie Madikizela - Mandela has again been at the centre of a controversy after her unexpected passing.

Link Macfarlane
Following the death of Winnie Madikizela-Mandela on easter monday, a documentary film about the former struggle stalwart’s life and times has sparked intense debate about Mam Winnie’s legacy.

Voice
The film, simply titled “Winnie”, was made by British filmmaker Pascale Lamche, and paints a different picture of Madikizela-Mandela to what many South Africans believed of her. The main revelations are that:
Vic Mcpherson, a director of Stratcom, an Apartheid unit that created false propaganda campaigns against struggle leaders, claimed to have targeted Winnie.
That Madikizela-Mandela was a thorn in the side of the ANC post 1994 because she disagreed with many of their policies
And that the murder investigations into Stompie Seipei and others was reopened in 1995 to continue the smear campaign against Winnie. Seipei was a young activist who fell foul of Winnie’s notoriously violent Mandela United Football Club.

Sound Up Dumisa
There is a shortage of balance in the documentary, and it does not do us any service.

Voice
Advocate Dumisa Ntsebeza, who was in charge of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s investigative unit, says the film leans too heavily on information given by former Stratcom operatives, the very people who made a living from twisting the truth.

Sound Up
We actually made a finding that Stratcom was responsible in some cases for people who got necklaced when they were innocent. And it was because of the disinformation.

Link Macfarlane
After 1994 many people thought that Mam Winnie would play a prominent role in the new democratic government, but the documentary on her has questioned the role that even her own party, the ANC, played in how she was portrayed to the public.

Voice
In 1995, when Madikizela-Mandela had a chance of becoming the deputy president of the ANC, the criminal investigations against her were suddenly reopened. Former Police Brigadier Henk Heslinga was the head of the Pretoria Murder and Robbery squad at the time. He says he was ordered to reopen the investigation by then Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi. We spoke to him via video conference in Kwa - Zulu Natal.

Sound Up Henk
So I went to Minister Sydney Mufamadi’s office and there he requested me that I must put up a task team and then we must investigate those allegations that is still hanging in the air about the murder cases where Winnie Mandela can be involved with.



Voice
On monday this week Mufamadi, who was not given a right of reply in the film, held a press conference to clear his name.

Sound Up Syndey Mufamadi
I am saying these investigations took place at the behest of Tony Leon, I’m talking about the ones with you, right, they took place at the behest of Tony Leon.

Sound Up Dumisa
There had been a request for this re-investigation by a member of the opposition party in the country, and that is quite legitimate.

Voice
Filmmaker Pascale Lamche, who was at the press conference, said Mufamadi’s statements backed up what the film portrayed.

Sound Up Pascale Lamche
My conclusions from this press conference is that, everything I say in the film was sustained. That the minister knew Henk Hesslinga, knew of these investigations, probably initiated them since it was such an enormous investigation, that it was incredibly costly, that it was a cross frontier investigation, that it lasted several months, he sustained all of that.

Voice
But Mufamadi said the narrative would have turned out different if he’d been given an opportunity to tell his side of the story.

Sound Up Sydney
People who would have something to tell, that is based on first hand knowledge, are not deemed to be important enough to feature in the documentary.

Voice
And that, says Adv Ntsebeza, leaves us with a very one sided view of our history.

Sound Up Dumisa
The legitimacy of the legacy of Nelson Mandela, with all his faults, with all his faults, is now being called into question. That is what an uncritical presentation of our history has caused.

Voice
Heslinga says the Murder and Robbery men never had anything to do with the intelligence work performed by units such as Stratcom.

Sound Up Henk
They were the James Bond people. We didn’t know what they were doing. We were not even allowed into their offices in Soweto. We had to sit and wait on the outside and wait for them if we wanted to see one of their investigators.

Voice
And he doesn’t see any reason to question the motives behind the reopening of the case against Madikiela-Mandela.

Sound Up Henk
Henk: From Sydney Mufamadi’s side I don’’t know if there was any political pressure or any political interference. But for me, as a senior police officer during those days, it wasn’t strange that the minister requested us to do an investigation into Winnie Mandela because she was a very… there was a lot of information hanging around that were never proved against her.

Link Macfarlane
Many of the freedom’s we enjoy today, such as the fact that we live in a free and equal society, were merely dreams back in the 70’s and 80’s. It’s easy to forget that at the time Mam Winnie was at the forefront of the struggle against Apartheid. She witnessed the brutality of the state on a daily basis.

Sound Up Winnie
I was terribly harassed. And I led a totally abnormal life. My house was nothing more then a police station. Those knocks at the door… Those vicious kicks at the door. Bangs on the windows. And I couldn’t predict when the police would come.

Sound Up Tokyo Sexwale
She heard the gunfire in Soweto. It’s a few meters from the house. When they murdered a child of thirteen, Hector Pietersen, and mowed down others throughout the country, she’s the woman, she stood.

Voice
Former Premier of Gauteng and long time personal friend of Winnie’s, Tokyo Sexwale, spoke to Carte Blanche a few days after her death. He said people were too eager to judge a woman who had spent most of her life fighting what had amounted to a war.

Sound Up Tokyo
When Sharpeville happens, she’s there. When Boipatong happens, she’s… every massacre, she saw these things.

Voice
Julius Malema has also spoken out in Winnie’s defence, lambasting her detractors while speaking at her funeral.

Sound Up Julius Malema
The cabal that rejected you, and disowned you, and sent you to the brutal Apartheid regime is here. Mama, you never told me how we must treat them when they come here.I’m waiting for a signal mam.

Voice
It doesn’t matter on which side of the argument you stand - the past few weeks have highlighted the fact that we still know very little of our own past. Dr Marjorie Jobson, of the Khulumani Support Group, has spent her life battling to help victims of Apartheid.

Sound Up Marjorie
The people who most needed the TRC, never reached the TRC. You know it was a very good process, but there is so much that was opened up, on all sides of this conflict, that its not been resolved.

Voice
Jobson wants government to do more to compensate the thousands of victims of Apartheid. She says the fact that both the previous regime and the new democratic leadership had to make concessions to keep the dream of a rainbow nation alive, hampered the TRC process.

Sound Up Marjorie
You know the real problem is that there are many, many people who know the truth. And the threats against the new government were if you follow up on any of these prosecutions we will reveal all the dirt we have on you. And that is all that has held up the process.

Voice
In a press release by Douglas Gibson, on behalf of Tony Leon who’s father had recently passed away, Gibson said: “Tony Leon was doing his job and any allegation that he was “behind” the persecution of Winnie Madikizela-Mandela is also a lie.” And while we may never know the whole truth about our complicated past, Advocate Ntsebeza says we should be extremely wary of who we allow to inform our opinions.

Sound Up Dumisa
Isn’t it time for South Africa to take a step back and say: who is reaping fruits of this dis-unity? Even in the language in which we now express what the liberation struggle by the ANC was all about… Is it Stratcom?
